evidenceKeys.docs: Cursor docs fetched as Markdown into .audit/pstack-parity-2026-11-05/cursor-docs/ (SHA256SUMS, RETRIEVED_AT)
evidenceKeys.builtin: Cursor built-in skills synced by the CLI into ~/.cursor/skills-cursor/
evidenceKeys.earlier: A capture recorded by an earlier run of this program (path given); not re-observed in this run
evidenceKeys.pi-e2e: Real Pi 1.5.0 CLI or RPC with the deterministic scripted test model (extensions/pi-pstack/test/e2e)

mechanisms.cursor: Plugin skills/ are discovered recursively; model-invocable skills are listed to the agent; disable-model-invocation hides a skill from automatic use; user-invocable:false and metadata.surfaces filter the slash menu (5622.index.js parseSkillMarkdown).
mechanisms.pi: Pi package skills from package.json pi.skills; Pi's Agent Skills loader honors disable-model-invocation. pstack sets no user-invocable or surfaces fields.
evidence: pi-unit: test/resources.test.ts loads all 79 skills with Pi loadSkills
pi-e2e: test/e2e/skills-catalog.e2e.test.ts attaches every skill body

mechanisms.feature: /name attaches a skill to one message
mechanisms.cursor: Every /name at the start or after whitespace that names a skill attaches it to the submitted message, each once (findSkillReferences, regex (?:^|\s)/([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)); interactive and headless submit paths both use it, alongside command expansion.
mechanisms.pi: input handler: expands a leading prompt template when skills are also referenced, then the first referenced skill rides Pi's /skill:name expansion and each further skill is a skill block ahead of the message.
mechanisms.changedThisRun: Before this run only a leading /name attached a skill, and a leading prompt template dropped later skill references.

mechanisms.feature: Skill as a sticky Custom Mode
mechanisms.cursor: Option+Enter (IDE) or sticky invocation (CLI) enters a mode: entered notice plus the attached skill on the first turn, a reminder on later turns, an exit notice once after leaving; badge from icon and color (custom-modes module).
mechanisms.pi: /mode <skill> [task], /mode off, /mode. Same notice texts; the skill block rides the system prompt on every request; badge in the footer.
evidence: docs: docs_skills.md Using a skill as a Custom Mode
pi-e2e: test/e2e/workflow.e2e.test.ts WORKFLOW-001 (mode reminder after a background poteto-agent run)
mechanisms.difference: The trigger is /mode instead of Option+Enter, and the skill sits in a system-prompt section instead of the entering user message. The model sees the same text.

mechanisms.cursor: rules/no-inline-imports.mdc and rules/typescript-exhaustive-switch.mdc with alwaysApply: true apply to every chat.
mechanisms.pi: Both rule bodies are injected verbatim into pstack_host on every request and are also /no-inline-imports and /typescript-exhaustive-switch skills.
mechanisms.changedThisRun: pi-pstack had prepended headings that the reference rule bodies do not have.

mechanisms.cursor: setup-pstack writes ~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc (alwaysApply). The CLI loads .cursor/rules from the workspace and every ancestor directory, so the home rule applies to workspaces under $HOME.
mechanisms.pi: setup-pstack writes <agent dir>/pstack/pstack-models.md; pi-pstack reads it before every request into pstack_models.
mechanisms.difference: Pi applies the rule in every workspace, and from the next request; the Cursor rule applies through the ancestor walk.

mechanisms.feature: Subagent types: built-ins and plugin agents
mechanisms.cursor: Agent files parse name, description, model (default inherit), readonly, is_background/background, tools, force-default-model. Built-in explore uses a faster model by default. The CLI enum also has shell, browser-use, computer-use and others; an earlier capture of CLI 2026.10.01 listed generalPurpose, explore, cursor-guide, ci-investigator, bugbot, security-review, best-of-n-runner plus plugin agents.
mechanisms.pi: generalPurpose and explore built-ins plus the four shipped agent files (name, description, model, readonly, is_background). explore defaults to the fast variant of the parent model.
mechanisms.difference: Cursor-internal types that pstack never names (cursor-guide, ci-investigator, bugbot, security-review, best-of-n-runner, browser) are not offered. team-kit's thermo-nuclear agent mentions subagent_type shell, which the observed CLI also does not list; a Task with shell fails in both.
mechanisms.changedThisRun: explore ran on the parent model.

mechanisms.cursor: Foreground returns the final text; background returns at once and enqueues a completion (title = first prompt line, 80 chars) that wakes the parent after its turn. Background runs are detached from the turn's abort signal.
mechanisms.pi: One pi --mode rpc child per agent; background children are not tied to the turn signal; completion arrives as a pstack/task notification after the turn.

mechanisms.cursor: CLI: resume of a finished agent continues it; resume while it runs fails with 'Sub-agent is currently running...'; lineage must match. pstack text describes steering a running agent, which the CLI does not do.
mechanisms.pi: Resume continues a finished agent; resume of a running agent steers the prompt into its run (pstack's described behavior); lineage is checked by workspace records.
mechanisms.difference: Follows pstack's described steer instead of the CLI's refusal.

mechanisms.cursor: The CLI rejects forkAgentId ('not supported in agent-cli subagents'); CreateAgentArgs fork_from and fork_turns exist for cloud agents.
mechanisms.pi: fork and fork_turns start a new agent from a copy of an idle agent's transcript in its directory.
evidence: pi-e2e: test/e2e/task.e2e.test.ts (fork of a worktree descendant)
mechanisms.difference: Pi offers locally what Cursor offers only for cloud agents; a fork needs an idle source.

mechanisms.cursor: readonly sends the child prompt in ASK mode and restricts its resources (5622.index.js executeSubagentOnce); docs: no file edits, no state-changing shell commands; strips MCP.
mechanisms.pi: readonly children get read, grep, find, ls and an OS-sandboxed read-only shell, no edits, no MCP.
mechanisms.difference: Pi enforces with a sandbox that also blocks network; environment credentials are still inherited.

mechanisms.cursor: A cloud subagent runs on its own VM and branch, keeps running with the laptop closed, uses team MCP configuration (docs_subagents.md Cloud subagents).
mechanisms.pi: environment cloud creates a git worktree on branch pstack/<agent id> and a separate local Pi process.
mechanisms.difference: No remote VM, no laptop-off execution, no team MCP configuration. Pi has no hosted agent runtime.

mechanisms.cursor: inherit by default; listed slugs such as claude-opus-5-5-xhigh or grok-4.7-xhigh-fast; bracket parameters [effort=,fast=,context=]; an invalid slug fails with the allowed list.
mechanisms.pi: Pi model specs provider/id:level or id[effort=,fast=]; legacy Cursor slugs map to a Pi model and level; inherit, auto, inherit-parent, fast aliases; invalid values fail with the allowed list.
mechanisms.difference: Model availability is the Pi model registry's, not the Cursor account's; the default grok-4.7 code model resolves only where a grok-4.7 Pi model exists.

mechanisms.cursor: Images and videos are read and attached to the subagent's context.
mechanisms.pi: Images are attached; a video path is named for the agent because Pi models have no video input.
mechanisms.difference: No video input in Pi models.

mechanisms.cursor: GetAgentStatusArgs and StopAgentArgs exist in the CLI protos; pstack's orchestrate and autopilot playbooks probe and stop agents.
mechanisms.pi: agent_status and stop_agent tools.

mechanisms.cursor: Interactive: a question dialog. Headless print: rejected with 'Questions skipped by the user, continue with the information you already have'. Subagent: 'Subagent cannot ask questions'.
mechanisms.pi: Pi select and input dialogs with a typed Other answer; without a person, the same reject reasons.
mechanisms.changedThisRun: The no-person result used pi-pstack's own per-question wording.

mechanisms.cursor: Todo list with merge semantics; the list stays visible to the agent.
mechanisms.pi: TodoWrite with branch reconstruction, a TUI widget, and the list in every request's system prompt.

mechanisms.cursor: Plan mode restricts by instruction; CreatePlan writes ~/.cursor/plans/<name>-<id8>.plan.md with todos, isProject, phases; build from the plan card, and bare /plan re-opens the existing plan review card (onShowExistingPlan). Headless print auto-approves SwitchMode and returns CreatePlan success without a file.
mechanisms.pi: /plan and SwitchMode with a reduced tool set and sandboxed read-only shell; CreatePlan writes the same file shape under <agent dir>/pstack/plans; a select dialog offers build choices after CreatePlan and on bare /plan when a plan is saved.
mechanisms.difference: Pi enforces the restriction (network also blocked); print and JSON runs do not offer SwitchMode; the plan card is a dialog; build in cloud is a local worktree worker.
mechanisms.changedThisRun: Bare /plan now opens the review dialog when a plan file is already saved.

mechanisms.cursor: Built-in loop skill: fixed interval or agent-paced; runs the prompt once at arming; local mechanism is a background shell that echoes a sentinel; stops only when asked; cloud uses cursor-subscriptions timers.
mechanisms.pi: /loop command and Loop tool with the same parse rules; an aborted tick no longer stops the loop.
mechanisms.difference: Pi schedules natively instead of through a sentinel shell; cloud cron timers are local supervisor timers.
mechanisms.changedThisRun: An aborted tick stopped the loop.

mechanisms.cursor: Shell moves to the background (block_until_ms 0 or after the wait), writes terminals/<id>.txt with header and footer, notifies on completion and on RE2 output matches.
mechanisms.pi: bash_background and AwaitShell with the captured texts and the original RE2 monitor rules.
mechanisms.difference: No approval gate or Cursor sandbox policy; a subagent's jobs end with the subagent process.

mechanisms.cursor: Cloud agents get cursor-subscriptions tools: subscribe_timer (delaySeconds or cron), subscribe_github_ci, subscribe_origin_ci, unsubscribe, list_subscriptions; Projects can also listen to Slack channels.
mechanisms.pi: subscribe_timer, subscribe_github_pr (covers checks), subscribe_webhook, list_subscriptions, unsubscribe, run by a local detached supervisor.
mechanisms.difference: Local supervision instead of hosted; no Origin CI or Slack channel subscriptions; the machine must stay on.

mechanisms.feature: Cursor Automations (Benny) and Grok Bot routines (make-bot-ui)
mechanisms.cursor: Hosted automations with Slack, schedule, and GitHub triggers created through /automate; webhook routines at api2.cursor.sh with update_state and SendToUser secret requests.
mechanisms.pi: Benny runs as subscriptions (cron sweep or local webhook) in a Pi session; make-bot-ui uses a loopback routine URL with a key in a local credential file.
mechanisms.difference: No hosted trigger service, no Slack event trigger, no public routine URL, no SendToUser secret prompt. Live Slack runs were not exercised (missing access).

mechanisms.cursor: Projects run a cloud coordinator with synced shared context; the system prompt names the agent store and Project paths.
mechanisms.pi: Workspace folders for stores, projects (notes.md tracker and store), artifacts, and terminals named in pstack_host.
mechanisms.difference: Local folders shared by local agents only; no cloud coordinator or cross-machine sync.

mechanisms.cursor: ~/.cursor/projects/<slug>/agent-transcripts/ JSONL, named in the system prompt.
mechanisms.pi: Pi session files and pi-pstack subagent transcripts, named in pstack_host; skill text describes Pi's entry format; worktree-audit.sh scans them.

mechanisms.cursor: Image generation; the interactive CLI shows a generate-image decision where the user can edit or approve the description.
mechanisms.pi: GenerateImage on Pi image models when one is available, saving to the artifacts folder.
mechanisms.difference: No approval step (Pi runs tools without approvals); offered only with an image model.

mechanisms.cursor: pr-review-canvas opens the page in Cursor's in-app browser; Canvas renders React artifacts beside the chat.
mechanisms.pi: The system browser, or control-ui for automated inspection.
mechanisms.difference: Pi has no embedded browser or canvas surface.

mechanisms.cursor: ketchup names a chart or diagram from /visualize. Neither the CLI bundle nor the fetched docs define it.
mechanisms.pi: visualize tool: bar or line chart as Unicode plus an SVG file.

mechanisms.feature: Inline screenshots and video in replies
mechanisms.cursor: Chat embeds screenshots and videos (ketchup, ketchup-video).
mechanisms.pi: The read tool shows images in capable terminals; video opens in the system player with frames read into the reply.
evidence: pi-e2e: test/e2e/skills-catalog.e2e.test.ts carries the adapted text
mechanisms.difference: Pi chat renders no inline image or video.

mechanisms.cursor: User info states Today's date.
mechanisms.pi: pstack_host states it in the same form.

mechanisms.cursor: ~/.cursor/skills-cursor/create-skill/SKILL.md
mechanisms.pi: skills/create-skill adapted to Pi skill locations.
mechanisms.difference: Pi skill locations and frontmatter instead of Cursor's.

mechanisms.feature: gh, Origin, Bugbot, agentic security review
mechanisms.cursor: Playbooks use gh by default and origin pr when command -v origin succeeds; Bugbot and security review comments are GitHub review threads.
mechanisms.pi: Same skill text and scripts (watch-pr parses Bugbot and security review threads).
evidence: pi-unit: test/scripts.test.ts runs the watch-pr and check-plan suites (61 tests)
mechanisms.difference: Origin is not installed on this host, so the Origin branch is unexercised (missing access).

mechanisms.feature: MCP discovery for why and reflect
mechanisms.cursor: Available-tools map or the mcps/ directory.
mechanisms.pi: mcp__<server>__<tool> tools or pi mcp list.
evidence: pi-e2e: test/e2e/skills-catalog.e2e.test.ts carries the adapted text
mechanisms.difference: No authenticated MCP exchange was exercised (missing access).

mechanisms.cursor: Run modes gate shell, web, MCP, and image generation with approvals and a sandbox.
mechanisms.pi: Pi runs tools without approval prompts; pi-pstack sandboxes only readonly agents and plan mode.
mechanisms.difference: pstack text does not depend on approvals; Pi's permission model is the host's.
